pointer_heap_insert.prompt:
Open `structures/heap.c` and implement `heap_insert`.

Use the conceptual one-based array index `n + 1` even though the tree is pointer-based:

1. Handle insertion into an empty heap.
2. Find the highest set bit of index `n + 1`.
3. Ignore that leading bit; each remaining intermediate bit chooses left (`0`) or right (`1`) while walking to the parent.
4. Use the final bit to attach the new node on the correct side and set its parent link.
5. While the new key is smaller than its parent's key, swap keys and move upward.

The harness checks an empty insertion and concrete positions `8` and `9`, including level order, heap order, node count, and parent links. Any correct O(log n) path method and upheap implementation passes; exact bit-loop syntax is not graded.
pointer_heap_insert.hint: Write the target index in binary. After removing the leading `1`, all but the last bit walk to the parent; the last bit selects the new left or right child.

help.concept: A complete tree has the same positions as a one-based heap array. Binary index bits encode the unique root-to-position path.
help.hint_1: For index `8 = 1000₂`, walk left, left, then attach left.
help.hint_2: Swap keys during upheap rather than pointer subtrees; the complete-tree shape and parent links then remain unchanged.

question-5-problem.title: Question 5: Use the Array Index Without an Array
question-5-problem.bodyMarkdown:
### Required function

```c
HeapNode *heap_insert(HeapNode *root, size_t n, int value);
```

The nodes use pointers, but the shape is still a **complete binary tree**. Number its positions as a one-based array heap:

```text
          1
       /     \
      2       3
    /  \    /  \
   4    5  6    7
```

The next node occupies index `n + 1`.

### Concrete trace

Start with level order:

```text
[10, 20, 15, 30, 40, 50, 60]
```

Inserting `5` when `n = 7` targets index `8 = 1000₂`.

- Ignore the leading `1` that represents the root.
- The next `0` moves left to index `2`.
- The next `0` moves left to index `4`.
- The final `0` attaches index `8` as the left child of index `4`.

Then upheap swaps `5` past `30`, `20`, and `10`. The animation keeps node positions fixed so you can see that only keys move during upheap.### Pointer-path pseudocode

```text
HeapInsert(root, n, x):
    if n == 0: return new Node(x)

    index = n + 1
    bits = binary(index) without its leading 1
    current = root

    for every bit except the last:
        if bit == 0: current = current.left
        else:        current = current.right

    attach the new node using the last bit
    set newNode.parent = current
    upheap(newNode)
    return root
```

The binary representation has `Θ(log n)` bits. Walking the path and upheap each cross at most the heap height, so insertion is `O(log n)`.

heap-animation.title: Trace the Binary Path and Every Upheap Swap
heap-animation.context: **Concrete pointer execution:** insert `5` into the seven-node heap. The animation separates root, path, and attachment bits, then keeps the tree shape fixed while the key upheaps.

steps.title: Start with the seven-node complete heap
steps.body: The pointer tree occupies conceptual indices `1` through `7`. Its level order is `[10,20,15,30,40,50,60]`, and every parent key is no larger than its children.

steps.title: Decode index 8 as a root path
steps.body: `8 = 1000₂`. Ignore the leading `1`. The remaining bits are `0,0,0`: left from root, left again, then attach on the left.

steps.title: Separate path bits from the attachment bit
steps.body: For target index `8 = 1000₂`, remove the leading `1` for the root. Among the remaining `000`, the first two bits walk to the parent and the last bit chooses the new child side. Keeping these roles separate prevents walking one level too far.

steps.title: Walk to the parent using intermediate bits
steps.body: The first intermediate `0` moves from index `1` to index `2` (key `20`). The second moves to index `4` (key `30`). The last bit is reserved for attachment.

steps.title: Attach the new node at index 8
steps.body: The final bit is `0`, so create a left child under index `4`. Set both directions of the relationship: `parent->left = node` and `node->parent = parent`.

steps.title: Upheap swap 1: compare with 30
steps.body: The inserted key `5` is smaller than parent key `30`, so swap their keys. The nodes and pointers stay in the same positions; the moving key is now at index `4`.

steps.title: Upheap swap 2: compare with 20
steps.body: At index `4`, key `5` is smaller than its new parent key `20`. Swap again and move the `node` cursor to index `2`.

steps.title: Upheap swap 3: compare with 10
steps.body: At index `2`, key `5` is smaller than root key `10`. Swap once more. The cursor reaches the root, so the loop stops.

steps.title: Verify the final heap
steps.body: The final level order is `[5,10,15,20,40,50,60,30]`. The tree is still complete, parent links did not change, and every parent key is at most its children.

steps.title: The next index uses the neighboring path
steps.body: After eight nodes, index `9 = 1001₂`. The intermediate bits still walk left-left to index `4`, but the final `1` attaches the new node as the right child. No breadth-first scan is needed.

steps.title: Count path and upheap work
steps.body: A complete tree with `n` nodes has height `Θ(log n)`. Decoding/walking the index path takes O(log n), and upheap moves at most that many levels. Total insertion time is O(log n).
